mainTopic: כיסוי הדם: which materials may cover the blood, and רבא's teachings on אברהם's "dust and ashes"
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about כיסוי הדם. The word "וכסהו" includes fine materials like sawdust, lime and crushed brick, and the word "בעפר" leaves out coarse materials, metal filings and flour. Anything that is a type of earth is valid. רב מרי explains why we do not read the פסוק as a כלל ופרט, which would allow only real earth. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא teaches that the material must be something seeds can grow in. רבא calls that rule nonsense, but רב נחמן בר יצחק defends it from a ברייתא: a traveler in the desert grinds a gold coin instead of using sand, and a traveler on a ship burns his garment for ash. Gold counts because a פסוק calls it עפר, and ash counts because of בית הלל's proof in their argument with בית שמאי. A ברייתא then adds more valid materials. Finally, רבא teaches that אברהם's words "I am dust and ashes" earned his children אפר פרה and עפר סוטה. His second teaching about אברהם begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: "And cover it" includes fine materials
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list of fine materials that may be used for כיסוי הדם and learns them from the word "וכסהו".
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine carpenters' sawdust, lime, crushed potsherd, and a brick or barrel lid that was crushed may also be used. How do we know? The פסוק says "and cover it."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a list of materials that may be used to cover the blood. It learns all of them from the general word "וכסהו".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list began before this section, so we are joining it in the middle. All these items are fine and powdery like earth. The word "וכסהו" is read broadly, so it includes covering with more than plain dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: a clay lid or stopper of a barrel
"the verse teaches"; it introduces the source in the פסוק

phrases.english: and fine sawdust of carpenters,
and lime, and crushed potsherd,
a brick and a barrel lid that one crushed?
The verse says: "and cover it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine materials like sawdust, lime and crushed brick are valid for כיסוי הדם, learned from "וכסהו".

steps.title: "With earth" excludes coarse and unsuitable materials
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the inclusion. Coarse materials, metal filings, uncrushed brick and flour products are excluded by the word "בעפר".
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think I should also include coarse manure, coarse sand, metal filings, an uncrushed brick or lid, flour, bran and coarse bran. So the פסוק says "with earth."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets a limit so that not everything counts. The word "בעפר" shows that some materials do not work for covering the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 used "וכסהו" to widen the rule. Now "בעפר" narrows it again. Notice that the same brick and lid are valid when crushed (step 1) but not valid when left whole.

keyTerms.meaning: "one might think"; it sets up a mistaken idea that the פסוק then rejects
filings or shavings from metal vessels

steps.confusionAlert: The brick and lid appear in both lists. Crushed, they are valid. Uncrushed, they are not. The difference is whether they have become powder like earth.

phrases.english: One might think that I include
even coarse manure and coarse sand,
and filings of metal vessels,
and a brick and a lid that one did not crush,
and flour, bran, and coarse bran?
The verse says: "with earth."
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק: "and cover it with earth."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף זֶבֶל הַגַּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the inclusion made in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coarse materials, metal filings, uncrushed brick or lid, and flour products are not valid for כיסוי הדם, learned from "בעפר".

steps.title: Why include these and exclude those?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what rule decides which materials go in the included list and which go in the excluded list.
steps.simpleTranslation: What made you decide to include these and exclude those?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own lists. It is setting up the next step, which will explain the dividing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists are made of non-earth materials, so it looks arbitrary that one group is allowed and the other is not. The question asks for the principle behind the split.

keyTerms.meaning: "what did you see?"; it asks for the reason behind a choice

phrases.english: And what did you see
to include these
and to exclude those?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת אֵלּוּ וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis for dividing the materials in steps 1 and 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The rule that decides which materials are included and which are excluded

steps.title: Whatever is a type of earth is included
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק both includes and excludes, materials that are a kind of earth are included and materials that are not are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק included and also excluded, I include the things that are a type of earth and exclude the things that are not a type of earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The dividing line is whether a material counts as a type of earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וכסהו" shows that more than real earth is allowed. "בעפר" shows that the material must still be like earth. So fine, earthy materials pass and coarse or foreign materials fail. The usual explanation is that plants can grow in the valid materials.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse included and also excluded

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for כיסוי הדם is that the material does not have to be real earth, but it must be a type of earth.

phrases.english: Since the verse included and excluded,
I include these
which are a type of earth,
and I exclude those
which are not a type of earth.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Materials that are a type of earth are included and materials that are not are excluded.

steps.title: Why not read the verse as כלל ופרט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. "וכסהו" is a general term and "עפר" is a detail, so by the rule of כלל ופרט only actual earth should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: "and cover it" is a general term and "earth" is a detail. With a general term followed by a detail, the general term includes only what is in the detail. So earth is allowed and nothing else!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the way the ברייתא read the פסוק. It suggests a different rule of reading that would allow only real earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under כלל ופרט, the detail limits the general term completely. Read that way, sawdust, lime and crushed brick would all be invalid. This challenges the wider inclusion the ברייתא made in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: a general term followed by a specific detail
the general term includes only what the detail names

phrases.english: Say: "and cover it" is a general term,
"earth" is a detail,
a general term and a detail:
the general term contains only what is in the detail;
earth, yes; anything else, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ריבוי ומיעוט reading used in steps 1 to 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's inclusion of non-earth materials
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק is a כלל ופרט, the detail "עפר" limits everything to actual earth.

steps.title: A general term that needs its detail
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי answers that "וכסהו" is a כלל הצריך לפרט, and such a verse is not read with the כלל ופרט rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: That is because this is a general term that needs the detail, and any general term that needs a detail is not read with the rule of כלל ופרט.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי defends the ברייתא. He explains why the כלל ופרט rule does not apply to this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וכסהו" alone is not clear, since it could mean just putting a vessel over the blood. "בעפר" is needed to show that the covering must be a material that goes on the blood itself. Because the detail only explains the general term, it does not shrink it down to earth alone.

keyTerms.meaning: a general term that needs a detail to explain what it means
we do not expound it with that rule

steps.whatToRemember: The ריבוי ומיעוט reading stands, so materials that are a type of earth are valid. כלל ופרט does not apply when the general term needs its detail to be understood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading פסוקים. The כלל ופרט method is not used when the detail is needed just to explain the general term.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
Because it is a general term that needs the detail,
phrases.notes: "Cover it" alone might mean putting a vessel on top. "With earth" explains what kind of covering is meant.

phrases.english: and any general term that needs a detail
is not expounded with the rule of general term and detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה כְּלָל הַצָּרִיךְ לִפְרָט
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits where the rule applies: כלל ופרט does not apply to a כלל הצריך לפרט
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "וכסהו בעפר" is a כלל ופרט, so only actual earth is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: "וכסהו" needs "בעפר" to be understood, so כלל ופרט does not apply and the broader ריבוי ומיעוט reading stands.

steps.title: Only covering material that can grow seeds
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא teaches that you may cover the blood only with material in which seeds can be planted and will sprout.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught: you may cover the blood only with something you can plant in and that makes things grow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching opens a new topic: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא gives a narrow rule for what may be used to cover the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps allowed anything that is a kind of earth. This rule is much stricter: the material must be able to grow seeds.

keyTerms.meaning: covering (the blood of a wild animal or bird)

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught publicly:
One may cover only
with a material in which one plants and it sprouts.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about what counts as valid covering material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Covering is valid only with material that can grow seeds.

steps.title: רבא rejects the teaching as nonsense
steps.stepSummary: רבא sharply rejects רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the new rule and calls it absurd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's problem is that earlier sources allow covering with materials in which nothing grows. So a rule that requires growing material seems to go against them.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is nonsense!
phrases.notes: He means earlier sources already allowed covering with things where nothing grows.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's rule that only material that grows seeds is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other sources allow materials in which nothing grows, so the rule seems absurd.

steps.title: Defending the rule with a ברייתא about travelers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says he himself gave this rule, and he based it on a ברייתא: a desert traveler grinds a gold coin rather than using sand, and a ship traveler burns his garment for ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: what's nonsense about it? I told it to him, and I based it on this ברייתא: someone in the desert with no ash grinds a gold coin and covers. Someone on a ship with no earth burns his garment and covers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the rule and shows its source in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The desert is full of sand, yet the ברייתא tells the traveler to grind gold instead. That shows sand, where nothing grows, is not valid. So the rule from step 7 has a real source.

keyTerms.meaning: a teaching of the תנאים; here, a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
What is nonsense about it?
I said it to him,
and I said it to him based on this baraita:
If one was traveling in the desert,
and he has no ash to cover with,
he grinds a gold coin and covers.
phrases.notes: The desert has plenty of sand, but he can't use it, because nothing grows in it.

phrases.english: If he was traveling on a ship,
and he has no earth to cover with,
he burns his garment and covers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's attack by showing the rule's source.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that covering material must be able to grow seeds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that makes the desert traveler grind gold instead of using sand.

steps.title: How does a gold coin count as earth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: ash is known to be called עפר, but where do we learn that ground gold counts?
steps.simpleTranslation: Burning the garment makes sense, because we found that ash is called earth. But a gold coin, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at the ברייתא and asks for a source for using ground gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ash case is fine because a source calls ash עפר. Gold is different, so the גמרא needs a פסוק that calls gold עפר too.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense that... (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: It makes sense that he burns his garment and covers,
since we found that ash is called earth,
but a gold coin, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ground gold counts as עפר.

steps.title: A פסוק calls gold dust
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a פסוק from איוב that speaks of "dust of gold."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: the פסוק says "and it has dust of gold."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question with a פסוק that uses the word עפר for gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says עפרות זהב, "dust of gold." Since a פסוק calls gold עפר, ground gold counts as עפר and may be used to cover the blood.
steps.whatToRemember: Ash and ground gold both count because a פסוק calls them עפר. Desert sand does not count because nothing grows in it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
"And it has dust of gold."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְעַפְרוֹת זָהָב לוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "ועפרות זהב לו" calls gold עפר.

steps.title: בית שמאי: only real earth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes בית שמאי: you may cover only with earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: you may cover only with earth. These are the words of בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא, starting with בית שמאי's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי limit covering to actual earth. This sets up a debate about whether ash also counts.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may cover only with earth,
these are the words of Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין מְכַסִּין אֶלָּא בְּעָפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that is the source for "ash is called earth" from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, only actual earth may be used to cover.

steps.title: בית הלל: ash is called earth
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל prove from the פרה אדומה פסוק that ash is called עפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: we found ash that is called earth, as it says, "And they shall take for the impure one from the earth of the burning."
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל disagree and bring a פסוק to show that ash may also be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the ashes of the burned פרה אדומה עפר. So ash is a kind of עפר and is valid for covering. This is the source the גמרא relied on in step 10.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
We found ash that is called earth,
as it says: "And they shall take for the impure one
from the earth of the burning."
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:17, about the ashes of the פרה אדומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים מָצִינוּ אֵפֶר שֶׁקָּרוּי עָפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with בית שמאי's view in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: Ash may be used for covering.

steps.title: בית שמאי: only "earth of burning," not plain earth
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that the פסוק calls ash "earth of burning," not plain "earth."
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי answer: it is called "earth of burning," but it is not called plain "earth."
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק needs the extra word "burning" to call ash עפר. Covering requires plain עפר, so ash still doesn't qualify.
steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי agree the פסוק uses the word עפר for ash. They only argue that it is a special, labeled kind of עפר, not plain עפר.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai respond:
It is called "earth of burning,"
but plain "earth" it is not called.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית הלל's proof from step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the פרה אדומה פסוק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק calls ash only "earth of burning," with an added word, never plain עפר.

steps.title: More materials that may be used to cover the blood
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds coal dust, eye-paint powder and chisel shavings to the list of things you may use for כיסוי הדם. Some add arsenic too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: they added to the list coal dust, stibium, and shavings from chiseling. Some say: even arsenic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds more materials to the earlier ברייתא's list of things you may use to cover the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא expounding וכסהו listed earth-like materials. This ברייתא adds more powdery or crumbly materials that also count as covering material - תוספות notes that הוסיפו עליהן refers to that earlier ברייתא, not the משנה. A second opinion, יש אומרים, adds arsenic as well.

keyTerms.meaning: They added to them (to the earlier ברייתא's list)
Stibium, a powder used as eye paint
Shavings that fall off when chiseling stone

phrases.english: It was taught: they added to them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the list of covering materials in the earlier ברייתא, not the משנה.

phrases.english: coal dust, and stibium,
and shavings from chiseling,
and some say: even arsenic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of ash and gold dust, the גמרא adds more valid covering materials from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coal dust, stibium and chisel shavings may be used for כיסוי הדם; according to יש אומרים, arsenic may be used too.

steps.title: אברהם's humility earned two מצוות of dust and ash
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that because אברהם אבינו said 'I am dust and ashes,' his children received two מצוות: אפר פרה and עפר סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: As a reward for what אברהם our father said, 'And I am dust and ashes,' his children earned two מצוות: the ashes of the פרה אדומה and the dust of the סוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives an אגדה teaching: אברהם אבינו's humble words were rewarded with two מצוות for his descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם אבינו said two words about himself, 'dust' and 'ashes.' Each word matches one מצוה: 'ashes' matches אפר פרה, and 'dust' matches עפר סוטה. This is a reward that fits the words he said.

keyTerms.meaning: The ashes of the פרה אדומה, used to make a טמא person טהור
The dust put into the water a סוטה drinks

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: covering the blood also uses earth, so why is it not counted as a reward too?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
phrases.english: Rava said: As a reward for what Avraham our father said:
"And I am dust and ashes,"
his children earned two מצוות:
the ashes of the red heifer, and the dust of the sotah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halachic list of covering materials to an אגדה about dust and ash.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם אבינו's words 'dust and ashes' earned his children the מצוות of אפר פרה and עפר סוטה.

steps.title: Why not count the earth used to cover blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: covering the blood also uses earth, so it should be counted as a third reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him also count the earth used for covering the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's list of only two מצוות, since כיסוי הדם also uses עפר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reward is מצוות that use dust, then כיסוי הדם should be included, because it is also done with עפר. So why did רבא say only two?

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal

phrases.english: But let him also count the earth for covering the blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's count of only two מצוות.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that only two מצוות came as the reward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כיסוי הדם also uses עפר, so it seems it should be counted as a third reward.

steps.title: Covering the blood gives no real benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the earth for covering blood helps do a מצוה, but it gives no benefit to a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there is a preparation for a מצוה, but there is no benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: עפר כיסוי הדם is different from the other two because it brings no benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward for אברהם אבינו was מצוות that actually help people. אפר פרה makes a טמא person טהור, and עפר סוטה can bring peace between husband and wife. Covering the blood is done after the animal is already slaughtered, so it is part of a מצוה but does not give any benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that helps carry out a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that covering the blood is less of a מצוה. It only says that it does not give a person a benefit, so it does not fit this kind of reward.
steps.whatToRemember: The two rewarded מצוות of dust and ash are ones that bring real benefit: טהרה from אפר פרה, and peace at home from עפר סוטה.

phrases.english: There, there is a preparation for a מצוה,
but there is no benefit.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a מצוה that brings benefit vs. a מצוה with no benefit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any מצוה done with dust should count as part of the reward.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only מצוות of dust and ash that give real benefit count; כיסוי הדם gives none.

steps.title: רבא begins another teaching about אברהם's words
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts a second teaching about a reward for something אברהם אבינו said. The teaching continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: As a reward for what אברהם our father said...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: רבא begins a new teaching about the reward for something else אברהם אבינו said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only opens the teaching. The words of אברהם אבינו and the reward for them come right after this line. It follows the same pattern as Step 16.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
phrases.english: And Rava said: As a reward for what Avraham our father said

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בִּשְׂכַר שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second אגדה teaching of רבא in the same pattern as Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening only; the content continues on the next amud.
